output.brief:
The rise in VA-220 failures comes from Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not from the new installers or firmware 4.2. A lab teardown found the internal seal deformed and unseated in 38 of 41 returned valves. Claim rates for Pellacott valves are the same across installer and firmware groups (about 41–42 per 1,000). Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 per 1,000 in every group. A helium retest of never-installed Pellacott 2026 stock found 11% leaking, against 1% for 2025 stock.

Pellacott's leak-test certificates do not reflect real tests. The test rig has been out of service since 9 Jan 2026 and was last used in December 2025. No VA-220 program is loaded on the other rigs, and 31 of 36 certificates repeat four old value sequences. Pellacott's score rose because the scoring rewards submitted paperwork, and that is what earned dock-to-stock.

Next steps:
- Keep the six lots on hold and do not accept fresh certificates.
- Quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott stock and suspend dock-to-stock.
- Run helium testing before releasing any lot, and consider shifting volume to Durrant-Hale.
- Drop the installer remediation and chargeback plan.
- Verify test records at other suppliers.

I'm confident in the main finding. The seal-versus-assembly-line cause is still unresolved, so don't pick a fix on that yet.
